## F-2 re-run — faceNeighbours' kept map

```
MK  keptMap returns the map whatever its key        boundary rc=1 (1 failed | 12 passed (13))  × is kept per arena and level by version and slot counts …
MK2 the neighbour claim's onFace re-check deleted   boundary rc=1 (1 failed | 12 passed (13))  × refuses a kept neighbour whose face slot now holds another region …
MS  the self claim's re-check deleted               boundary rc=1 (1 failed | 12 passed (13))  × refuses a kept entry naming the face itself …
MN  "no face" claims never checked                  boundary rc=1 (3 failed | 10 passed (13))  × between a batch's writes and its commit … · × … once a record owns that ring · × … across a hole ring …
MAN the face-record comparison (sameAnchors) deleted boundary rc=1 (2 failed | 11 passed (13))  × … once a record owns that ring · × … across a hole ring …
MRW the ring walk's mapped-face test deleted        boundary rc=1 (1 failed | 12 passed (13))  × between a batch's writes and its commit … (line 220: `[]` for `[1]`; the sidesFirst arena, by elimination)
MLV onFace's liveness test dropped                  boundary rc=0 (13 passed (13))  → survives: N-7
```

I read `neighbours.ts` whole to check that the re-check is complete. A kept claim "f across g" is accepted only when f
is live and g lies on f's rings now. "The face itself across g" is accepted only when g lies on the face's own rings
now. "No face across g" is accepted only when two things hold. First, every face record of the level (its liveness,
outer and hole anchors) is the one the map was built from. Second, no half-edge on g's ring, walked now, was mapped to
a face. Any face that owns g's ring now has an anchor on that ring. With the records unchanged, that face owned the
anchor at build time, so the map holds it there and the check refuses.

So on an arena whose live records own disjoint rings, every kept answer equals a fresh build's. That covers every
committed arena, and every batch state that keeps one record per region. CONFIRMED for the probe states by tests and
mutants; PLAUSIBLE (reasoned) in general.

The one state outside that premise is a ring claimed by two live records. It is a transient inside a batch that
allocates a region's new record before freeing the old one. There the answer depends on history (probe P2, below);
that is N-8, not a blocker. The guarantee is recorded in C-0163, which names C-0159 (6) and supersedes nothing.

## Verdict: FAIL — three failing lines (F-1, F-2, F-3), each small; six notes

The services are built, exported under the design's names, and green under every gate. Their readings of the open
cases are recorded in C-0159. The code reads well against §3.1, §3.4 and §4.6. The failures are tests that cannot
fail on claims the item makes. Each one was shown by a mutant that survives the test meant to hold the claim.

* **F-1** (checklist line 3, a silently narrowed bar). Four of the B-FUZZ properties in `bfuzz.test.ts` claim checks
  that their bodies do not make. These are the properties for hexLattice, regularFit, sampleBoundary and the curves.
  At the nightly size of 10⁶, then, "0 invalid outputs" is not judged on those claims. Mutants MA – MD each pass
  `bfuzz.test.ts`. CONFIRMED.
* **F-2** (checklist line 2, a choice clause with no test). C-0159 (6) says faceNeighbours' cache is "cached per
  arena by version and slot counts … a stale map rebuilds, never answers". No test changes an arena after a query, so
  the cache's invalidation and its re-check are never exercised. MK (the cache never invalidated) and MK2 (no
  re-check) both pass every test of the item. CONFIRMED.
  The claim is also not what the code does when the tables change while the version and the slot counts stay the
  same. A probe gives a missed neighbour: `[]` where a fresh map gives `[1]`. CONFIRMED. Whether any caller can query
  in that window (between a batch's writes and its commit) is M0-a-06's design: PLAUSIBLE.
* **F-3** (checklist line 2, a choice clause with no test). C-0159 (4) replaces a fillet arc by its virtual corner
  only when the short runs "bend one way through more than the tolerance". Only the positive case is tested. ME (no
  tolerance guard) and MF (no one-way check) both pass `side-runs.test.ts` and `bfuzz.test.ts`. CONFIRMED.

**Required change.** Make each of the four properties assert what its title claims:
* hexLattice: every point strictly inside the region (even–odd), and no two points equal.

the region", which is hexLattice's core validity. Re-run MA – MD against `bfuzz.test.ts` alone: each must turn it red.

### F-2 — faceNeighbours' cache (C-0159 (6)) has no test that can fail, and its "never answers" claim does not hold for an unbumped version

`neighbours.ts` keeps a half-edge → face map per arena and level in a `WeakMap`. Its key is the version plus a
fingerprint of slot counters: `pair.top/live`, `face[level].top/live`, `vertex.top` and `holesTop[level]`. A cached
neighbour is re-checked by `onFace` before it is returned. Every test builds a fresh arena (a new `Plat`, so an
empty cache) and never changes its topology after a query. The one commit test, `boundary.test.ts:81`, bumps the
version with nothing changed. So no test can see either mechanism fail:

```
MK  neighbours.ts:57 `if (!fresh && m !== undefined) return m;` (the map never invalidated)
MK  test/geom/boundary.test.ts rc=0 (Tests  6 passed (6))      MK  test/geom/bfuzz.test.ts rc=0 (Tests  11 passed (11))
MK2 neighbours.ts:88 the onFace re-check deleted
MK2 test/geom/boundary.test.ts rc=0 (Tests  6 passed (6))      MK2 test/geom/bfuzz.test.ts rc=0 (Tests  11 passed (11))
```

The re-check catches a wrong positive entry. It cannot catch a missed neighbour, because entries that read −1 (no
face) or the queried face itself are skipped and never checked. Probe P1 (source saved at
`…/scratchpad/waves/check-M0-a-10/probe-stale.test.ts`) builds two arenas on the same 20 × 10 m rectangle with the
same eight vertices and ten edges. In the first, E (x = 10 m) is at L0 and F (x = 5 m) at L1. In the second the
levels are reversed. That second arena is the state a batch that demotes E and promotes F reaches after its writes
and before its commit. Both arenas have the same version and fingerprint (`0|10/10/2/2/8/0`). The probe queries the
first arena, moves the second's tables into the same `Plat` object, and queries again:

```
before: p1 L0 neighbours of the left face  [1]
after (no commit): cached [] fresh [1]
after commitVersion:  [1]
```

After a commit the answer is right, because the version keys the map. Between the writes and the commit, the cached
answer silently misses a neighbour, and it depends on whether an earlier call filled the cache. That makes it a
determinism hazard across workers if such a call is ever made. The design gives services values "valid until the
next commit" (§3.4). §5.3's reachability walk uses faceNeighbours (§3.10). Whether any caller can query
mid-batch is M0-a-06's and M0-a-14's design, so the hazard is PLAUSIBLE. The test gap is CONFIRMED.

**Required change.**
1. Add tests that kill MK and MK2. MK needs a query, then a topology change on the same `Plat`, then
   `commitVersion`, then a query that must show the new neighbours. M0-a-02's raw allocators, or two built arenas as
   in P1, will do. MK2 needs a stale positive entry that the re-check must refuse.
2. Choose one of the following and record it in a new choices row that names C-0159 (6):
   * Make the re-check complete, so a mid-batch read cannot miss a neighbour. That means checking −1 and self
     entries against the half-edge's level and its ring; the arena's outer ring is no face.
   * Restate the guarantee as "answers for the committed arena; a call between a batch's writes and its commit is
     not supported", and have the session route that restriction to M0-a-06's and M0-a-14's briefs.

### F-3 — sideRuns' fillet-arc conditions (C-0159 (4)) have no test that can fail

C-0159 (4) reads "a crossing street's fillet arc is replaced by its virtual corner" (§4.6 *Sides*) as follows: a
maximal sequence of short runs between two long runs that "bends one way through more than the tolerance". The
item's test holds the positive case: an arc is collapsed (`side-runs.test.ts:62` and `:92`). No fixture holds the
negative cases, where short runs that are not a fillet must stay:

```
ME side-runs.ts:186 guard `if (!(Math.abs(theta) > tol)) return;` deleted
ME test/geom/side-runs.test.ts rc=0 (Tests  6 passed (6))      ME test/geom/bfuzz.test.ts rc=0 (Tests  11 passed (11))
MF side-runs.ts:191 one-way check deleted
MF test/geom/side-runs.test.ts rc=0 (Tests  6 passed (6))
```

Neither mutant is equivalent:
* Without ME's guard, two long runs whose chords differ by less than the tolerance can still be split apart by the
  band, which is measured from each run's first edge. Their short middle run would then collapse to the far meeting
  point of two nearly parallel lines.
* Without MF's check, a jog of short runs that turn both ways would collapse to a corner.

MG (the `sP > 0`, `tN < 1` check at `side-runs.ts:201`) also survives, but it is equivalent given ME's and MF's
checks. A chord chain that turns one way by less than π meets its end lines beyond its ends. One-line note; no test
needed. PLAUSIBLE (reasoned).

**Required change.** Add negative fixtures with `arcMaxCm > 0`, each of which must keep its short runs (no
`virtualStart` / `virtualEnd`, no run dropped):
* a notch or jog of short runs, turning both ways, between two long collinear runs;
* a gentle bend whose two long runs' chords differ by less than the tolerance, with a short run between them.

Re-run ME and MF: each must turn `side-runs.test.ts` red.
